_README: TEMPLATE for recording REAL GCF pipeline projects. Copy this file, rename it (e.g. data/gcf/real-projects.json),
replace the illustrative example values with the institution's real facts, then record them with:
Add --dry-run first to validate without writing anything.
Every key beginning with an underscore (like this one, and the _help notes below) is guidance only —
the recorder ignores them, so you can leave them in place while you fill in the real values.
The three projects below mirror the walk-through in the GCF Pipeline Playbook so you can see the shape:
one that passes every gate, one that is flagged, and one that is excluded. They are ILLUSTRATIVE — replace
the ids, names and every figure with the real projects before recording, or they will record as-is.

_vocabularies.resultsArea: One of: EP (energy access & power), LT (low-emission transport), BA (buildings/cities/industry/appliances), FL (forests & land use), VC (livelihoods of people & communities), HW (health/food/water security), IB (ecosystems & ecosystem services), EE (most vulnerable people & communities)
_vocabularies.stream: mitigation (reduces/avoids/removes emissions) or adaptation (builds resilience). An adaptation project is NEVER ranked on carbon.
_vocabularies.stage: concept, pre_feasibility, cn_drafted, cn_submitted, ppf, fp, fp_submitted, board, approved, faa, implementation, closed
_vocabularies.essCategory: A (significant/irreversible impacts — OUTSIDE DFCC's B/I-2 accreditation, will be excluded), B (limited, mitigable), C (minimal), or I-1/I-2/I-3 for on-lending portfolios
_vocabularies.tier: The evidence behind a figure: measured (metered/audited), modelled (calculated), benchmark (a published default), or declared (the sponsor's own statement). Not a PCAF score.
_vocabularies.baseline.type: reduced (project cuts existing emissions), avoided (emissions that would otherwise have happened), or removal (carbon taken out of the air). Decided by the counterfactual, not by the engine.
_vocabularies.instrument: One of the seven catalogue structures: concessional_credit_line, risk_sharing_facility, blended_sll, subordinated_debt, results_based_finance, green_bond_warehouse, fx_hedging_facility
_vocabularies.barriers: Why it is not already financed commercially: tenor, offtake_risk, currency, perceived_technology_risk, upfront_capex, no_revenue_stream, fragmented_borrowers

projects._help: PROJECT A — passes every gate. Replace all values with a real project.
projects.name: EXAMPLE A — Rooftop Solar for Commercial Estates (replace me)
projects._help_selectionReason: 40+ characters. Why this project, in the bank's own words. Required.
projects.selectionReason: Distributed rooftop solar on commercial estates that already carry DFCC facilities; a clean extension of an existing book with a known offtake.
projects.essNote: Rooftop installations on existing buildings; limited, site-specific, readily mitigated impacts.

financing.gcfInstrumentDetail: Concessional tranche on-lent through DFCC to extend tenor. No grant element.

viabilityWithoutGcf.reason: Commercial tenor tops out well short of the payback period on rooftop solar for these borrowers; GCF's tranche buys the missing years of tenor, not a margin subsidy.

annual_tCO2e.method: installed capacity x yield x grid emission factor

baseline.description: Grid electricity displaced at the Sri Lankan national average emission factor
baseline.counterfactual: Without the project the estates draw the same demand from the national grid

indirect.definition: People working on the served estates

projects._help: PROJECT B — flagged (a mandate question, not a rejection). Adaptation, so never ranked on carbon.
projects.name: EXAMPLE B — Coastal Aquaculture Resilience (replace me)
projects.selectionReason: Resilience of smallholder coastal aquaculture to warming and storm surge; a livelihoods project the NAP prioritises for the Eastern coast.
projects.essNote: Community-level works with a gender and stakeholder plan; no large infrastructure.

financing.gcfInstrumentDetail: Resilience outcomes are not paid for by any market; results-based finance is the structure that reaches them.

viabilityWithoutGcf.reason: The adaptation benefit has no buyer, so no commercial structure prices it. The only instrument that reaches it depends on the grant modality DFCC does not currently hold — a mandate question to verify with DFCC and the NDA.

annual_tCO2e.note: Adaptation project; mitigation is a co-benefit, not the objective, and is not the basis for ranking.

baseline.description: Not a mitigation project; no mitigation baseline is claimed
baseline.counterfactual: Resilience of livelihoods, measured in beneficiaries reached, not in tonnes
baseline.note: Type is a required field; for a pure adaptation project it carries no weight because no mitigation tonnage is claimed.

mitigation.coBenefitNote: Any emissions benefit is incidental to the resilience objective and sits on its own line.

indirect.definition: Wider coastal community dependent on the fishery

projects._help: PROJECT C — excluded. Category A is outside DFCC's B/I-2 accreditation. It keeps its row and its reason.
projects.name: EXAMPLE C — Cement Line Expansion with Efficiency Upgrade (replace me)
projects.selectionReason: A more efficient kiln per tonne of cement, brought as a mitigation project by the sponsor; recorded honestly so the gate can speak.
projects.essNote: A new cement line is a significant, category A industrial development.

viabilityWithoutGcf.reason: A commercial expansion the sponsor can finance; recorded to demonstrate the eligibility gate, not because it needs GCF support.

annual_tCO2e.method: intensity improvement per tonne, but output doubles so absolute emissions rise

lifetime_tCO2e.note: Negative because absolute emissions increase against the true counterfactual.

baseline.description: Per-tonne intensity improves, but the counterfactual is not 'the old kiln at the same output'
baseline.counterfactual: Without the project the market is not served by this doubled output at all; total emissions rise
baseline.note: The climate rationale fails on the counterfactual — an efficiency gain per tonne alongside a doubling of output is not an emissions reduction.
